deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §22 of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), on the zeros of the theta function on a compact Riemann surface T of genus p. The next page drafts the companion argument with log ϑ and the integral ∫ log ϑ du_μ around T'. The previous page and the letter at the bottom date the sheet to May 1857.

Setting. The u_μ (μ=1..p) are normalized everywhere-finite Abelian integrals. Normalized means they have periods πi δ_{μν} across the cuts a_ν and a_{μν} across the cuts b_ν. η_1,...,η_p are the p zeros on T of the function ϑ(u_1 − e_1, ..., u_p − e_p). Write α_μ^{(ν)} = u_μ(η_ν).

Step 1 (stated as already obtained). e_μ = Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} + k_μ, where k_μ depends only on T and on the normalization of u. These k_μ are Riemann's constants; the page refers to an earlier integral expression for them. Hence the function of the point (s,z) vanishing exactly at η_1..η_p is ϑ(u_1 − Σ_ν α_1^{(ν)} − k_1, ..., u_p − Σ_ν α_p^{(ν)} − k_p). That is, one substitutes v_μ = u_μ − Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} − k_μ into ϑ(v_1,...,v_p).

Step 2 (effect of the base point). The conditions defining u_μ (periodicity moduli only across the a-cuts, with the normalization) fix u_μ only up to an additive constant. Replace u_μ by u'_μ = u_μ + c_μ. The page reuses the letter k_μ for this shift, a slip. Then:
- α_μ^{(ν)} becomes α_μ^{(ν)} + c_μ;
- u_μ − Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} becomes u_μ − Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} − (p−1)c_μ, since the p-term sum gains p c_μ and u gains c_μ;
- so the same theta function reads ϑ(u' − Σα' − k'), with k'_μ = k_μ − (p−1)c_μ.

Step 3 (my completion of the deleted line, which says exactly this). Choose c_μ = k_μ/(p−1). This is possible for p ≥ 2. Then k'_μ = 0.

Conclusion. The additive constants of the u_μ (equivalently the lower limits of the defining integrals) can be fixed so that substituting v_μ = u_μ − Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} into ϑ gives a function vanishing to first order at η_1,...,η_p. Riemann remarks he will reach this normalization of the constants more easily by another route than through the integral formula for k_μ.

Finally he begins a definition: two systems (v_1..v_p), (v'_1..v'_p) are called congruent, i.e. congruent modulo simultaneous periods. This is the congruence notation of the published §22-23.

The lower part of the sheet is a draft of a personal letter: 'Lieber Ritter!', Göttingen 27 Mai 1857. He received two letters the previous evening at 9 o'clock that had not been forwarded from Göttingen, and answers in haste. It has no mathematical content.
errors: Notational slip: the same symbol k_μ is used both for the shift of the additive constant of u_μ and for Riemann's constant. Read literally, 'k_μ goes over into k_μ − (p−1)k_μ' is correct only for the shift c_μ = k_μ/(p−1), as the deleted line about K_μ = k_μ/(p−1) makes clear.
The division by p−1 requires p ≥ 2. For p = 1 the constant k is independent of the base point and cannot be removed this way. The page does not say this, but it is harmless.

The identities hold modulo periods, since k_μ (and the theta zero set) is only determined modulo the period lattice. The text treats them as equalities, which is fine given the congruence notation introduced immediately after.

results.what: The zeros η_1..η_p of ϑ(u − e) satisfy e_μ ≡ Σ_ν u_μ(η_ν) + k_μ, with k_μ independent of e.
results.modern_name: Riemann vanishing theorem / Riemann's constant vector

results.what: Under a change of base point (additive constant c in u), Riemann's constant transforms as k → k − (p−1)c, so for p ≥ 2 the base point can be chosen to make k ≡ 0.
results.modern_name: Base-point dependence of Riemann's constant vector (K_{P0} shifts by (g−1)(A(P1)−A(P0)))
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857, published in §22 of the Abel functions paper

results.what: Congruence of p-tuples modulo the simultaneous period lattice
results.modern_name: Points of the Jacobian C^p / lattice

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material that appears in Riemann's published 1857 paper (§22): the theta zero theorem, the removal of the constant k by choice of the integration constants, and the congruence notation. Nothing goes beyond the published text; the historical interest is only in the draft wording and the dated letter.

checkable.sympy: p,c,k,u=symbols('p c k u'); a=symbols('a1:6'); P=5; expr_old=u-sum(a)-k; expr_new=(u+c)-sum(ai+c for ai in a)-(k-(P-1)*c); simplify(expr_old-expr_new)==0
checkable.asserts: For p=5: shifting u and all α by c while replacing k by k−(p−1)c leaves the theta argument unchanged.
Choosing the shift c = k/(p−1) makes the new Riemann constant vanish.

transcription_corrections: The word read as 'Ableitungsconstante' is doubtful; in context it should mean the additive constant ('additive Constante'/'Additionsconstante') of u_μ. The machine reading is likely wrong.

In the line 'für u_μ auch die Function u_μ + k_μ', the shift symbol on the page is k_μ. The inserted '$\frac{k_\mu}{p-1}$' belongs to the deleted line 'und wenn K_μ = k_μ/(p−1) genommen wird verschwindet ...', not to this line.
The first formula should read e_μ = Σ_ν α_μ^{(ν)} + k_μ, with the summation over ν = 1..p.
In the letter, '... und ich bin nun ...' is better read as '... und kann Dir nun in aller Eile mit wenigen Worten darauf antworten' (approximately).
